paragraphs: Rabbi Shasha, son of Rabbi Abba. (Sheshai; Ezra.)[^1]

He is mentioned at the beginning of Shemot Rabbah, chapter 24: he would write the he below and the lamed above, in the word הלה׳ in the phrase “Is this how you repay the Lord?” Yuḥasin has the reading “bar Rava.” But the source of the midrash is the Yerushalmi, Megillah, chapter 1, halakhah 9, where the reading is “R' Yosha, son of Rav Chanael.” The Yerushalmi’s reading is the correct one, as Rav Chanael too is known to have been a scribe.[^2]

notes.text: The heading reads ששא, not ששת (Sheshet); Shasha is a transliteration of that unpointed spelling, not a claim to have established its vocalization. Hyman’s parenthesis reads ששי, עזרא פ״ד־כ. Sheshai represents ששי; the Ezra locator is kept here exactly as printed because its intended reference is unresolved.

רפ״כד means the beginning of chapter 24, rather than its end; ש״ר is rendered by the customary title Shemot Rabbah. The names יושע׳ and חנאל are kept distinct from the earlier English normalizations Yehoshua and Chananel. The Yuḥasin variant is printed בר רבא, rendered bar Rava. The relative positions of the letters, the preference for the Yerushalmi reading and the assertion that Chanael was a scribe are Hyman’s statements; the preference remains Hyman’s judgment. The checked Shemot Rabbah passage supports the full titles in the heading, but the checked Yerushalmi edition differs in the name, as explained below. The quoted Hebrew phrase is הלה׳ תגמלו זאת. The printed Yerushalmi locator is ה״ט־יא :; it is retained here exactly, without treating it as a range of halakhot or assigning a verified modern locus.

[Shemot Rabbah 24:1](https://www.sefaria.org/Shemot_Rabbah.24.1) explicitly reads Rabbi Shesha son of Rabbi Abba. In the checked Guggenheimer edition, [Jerusalem Talmud Megillah 1:9:10](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Megillah.1.9.10) instead reads רַב שֶׁשְׁעָה בְרֵיהּ דְּרַב חֲנַנְאֵל, Rav Shesh'a son of Rav Chananel. Hyman’s reported form יושע׳ is retained in the body as Yosha, with R' for its abbreviated title; neither the name nor its title is silently replaced from the other edition. The original printed locator and Yuḥasin variant remain as recorded above.
